title: Management Information Systems: Main Exam, 22 April 2021
department: Department of Information Technology / enterprise Computing
instructions: ANSWER ALL QUESTIONS IN QUESTION ONE AND ANY OTHER TWO.

parts.text: Distinguish the meaning of the following terms.
Information systems and management information systems
Tactical management and top management
Decision support system and executive support system
Why are transaction processing systems (TPS) considered to be the 'data lifeline' of a business?
Decisions in organizations can be termed as structured, semi-structured or unstructured. State the management levels at which these decisions are made.

Information systems in organizations interact with other stakeholders in the environment. Using a road construction company as an example, identify three stakeholders and indicate how they relate to the company.
Explain how executive information systems (EIS) help strategic managers in decision making.
Prototyping is a popular system development methodology. When is it necessary to use a prototype to build a system?
In the decision-making hierarchy of an organization, describe and give examples of the use of the following information system types.
Decision support systems (DSS)
Executive information systems (EIS)
Expert systems (ES)
Describe a DSS and outline its set of typical software components.
Illustrate how an organization can use a DSS to improve decision-making.
Using relevant examples, show how information technology has helped organizations achieve the following.
Cost reduction
Differentiation
Customer loyalty
Telecommunication networks have continued to play a key role in supporting business activities in organizations. Outline the motivation behind the increased use of telecommunication networks.
Outline four types of decisions that can be supported by a decision support system.
Discuss five moral dimensions of the information age that organizations are facing today in Kenya.
Outline the various information system threats bankers are facing today and how the challenge is being countered.

items.text: Transaction processing is a critical stage in the life of a transaction processing system (TPS).

parts.text: Identify and describe two approaches that can be used to process a transaction.
Describe the key steps of transaction processing.
Discuss six techniques that can be used to secure a TPS from intrusion.
